slides: Let's continue with circles, this time with the angles and the arcs.

slides.say: Now the angles in a circle. The first one is the inscribed angle. An inscribed angle is made by two chords that start at the same point on the circle. Let's take a point C on the circle, and draw two chords from it, to A and to B.
at: Now the angles in a circle

slides.say: Its vertex, the point of the angle, is on the circle. That's why it's called inscribed. And the angle is exactly between the two chords.
Here's another inscribed angle, and another one, a big one. In both, the vertex is on the circle.

But notice. If we just drew two lines and stopped somewhere in the middle of the circle, the vertex would be inside the circle. Or if they met out here, the vertex would be outside it. Those are not inscribed angles. An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle.

Now let's look at a central angle. You can guess this one from the name. Its vertex is at the center of the circle, at O. And it's between two radii. Here's a radius, and here's a radius, and the angle between them is a central angle.
It can be small, like forty-five degrees. It can be big, like a hundred twenty. And when the two radii make a straight line, a diameter, it's a central angle of a hundred eighty degrees.
at: when the two radii make a straight line

slides.say: An arc is a part of the circle, a piece of the round line. Let's mark a piece of the circle. That's an arc. An arc can be short. It can be longer. And it can be very long, almost the whole circle.
at: Let's mark a piece of the circle

slides.say: An arc can be closed off by a chord. Here's a chord, A B. It splits the circle into two arcs. There's the arc on this side, the short one. On the exam it's called the minor arc.

And there's another arc, a bigger one, all the way around the other side. That's the major arc. People often think an arc is always something short. But this whole long piece is an arc too, even though it's more than half the circle.
Now here's an arc, from A to B. We can close it off with two radii. That's a central angle that closes off our arc.

When an angle meets an arc at both ends like this, we say that the angle intercepts the arc. Here the central angle has its vertex at O. Its two radii end at A and B. The blue arc between A and B is the arc it intercepts.
at: Its two radii end at A and B

slides.say: An inscribed angle can intercept that same arc. Take a point C on the other side of the circle, on the long arc, away from the blue arc. Draw two chords from C to A and to B. The angle at C intercepts the blue arc A B, the arc opposite C, not the arc that passes through C.
So this central angle and this inscribed angle both intercept the same arc, the blue arc A B. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
